subject: POC runway padding — integration sprint slip & extension request
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@brightbridge.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: POC runway padding — integration sprint slip & extension request

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the quick demo earlier this week. The BrightBridge team is making great progress on the UI side, but Karthik flagged a couple of adapter edge cases that are going to consume the rest of this sprint.

High level: the POC is blocked on two integration items (auth token rotation + streaming backpressure) that will take ~2–3 weeks to resolve on your side. Given that, we want to propose a short extension to the POC runway and a small sandbox token refill so your engineers can finish validation without the token limit gating the tests.

Ask:
- 45-day extension to the current sandbox window (to preserve your evaluation cadence)
- 100k token credit top-up for the BrightBridge sandbox

I attached a short log excerpt showing the rotation error (integration-error-excerpt.txt) and Karthik has included a proposed runbook below. If this works for you we will route this through our internal approvals and procurement — we usually approve these bridge credits for integration blockers.

Next steps: if you confirm we have permission to escalate to finance/procurement, I’ll initiate the approval and loop Marissa for the billing paperwork.

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192
From: Sara Lim <sara.lim@brightbridge.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightbridge.ai
Date: Sat, 05 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC runway padding — integration sprint slip & extension request

Hi David —

Appreciate the transparency. We discovered the auth token rotation behavior late in QA when we ramped load; that explains the intermittent failures we saw in the demo scenarios.

A couple of quick notes from our side:
- We can commit the engineering time to resolve the two blockers, but our release calendar pushed the fix to the end of the month (hence the 2–3 week slip).
- Procurement asked whether this is a formal extension (changed end date) or a temporary token refill. They prefer a single doc that covers both so they can approve quickly.

Can you share the approval path (who signs the refill) and what the billing implications are if we accept the 100k token top-up? Also include any minimal acceptance criteria you'd like us to hit so procurement understands success gating.

Thanks — I’ve CC’d procurement for visibility.

Best,
Sara Lim
Head of Integrations | BrightBridge Analytics
sara.lim@brightbridge.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sara Lim <sara.lim@brightbridge.ai>
Date: Mon, 07 Sep 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC runway padding — integration sprint slip & extension request

Quick technical summary (since Sara asked for acceptance criteria):

Root causes identified:
- Token rotation race: client library retries can cause stale tokens to be used when rotations overlap (seen in logs, attached excerpt).
- Backpressure handling: streaming payloads under burst expose a race that drops some frames — causes partial responses.

Fix plan (estimated):
- Week 1: token rotation guard + unit tests (BrightBridge engineering)
- Week 2: streaming backpressure fix + integration tests (joint tests with Redwood)
- Week 3: validation, smoke runs, and demo replay to confirm metrics

Proposed acceptance criteria to share with procurement:
- Successful end-to-end demo with the same dataset + no auth errors for 24h soak test
- Median tail latency within the agreed POC SLO for the demo traffic pattern
- Repro script and logs (to be uploaded to shared Drive)

Attachments: integration-runbook.pdf 

If procurement prefers, we can split the approach into: 30-day extension + 100k tokens, with an option to extend to 45 days if we hit roadblocks. From an engineering perspective the 45-day buffer is safer, but we can be flexible if finance needs smaller increments.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lim <sara.lim@brightbridge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, procurement@brightbridge.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC runway padding — integration sprint slip & extension request

Sara —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. I’ll start the internal approval flow today and loop Marissa for the billing doc. To be transparent about what we typically need for these requests:

Standard approval package we’ll submit to finance:
- Brief rationale (engineering blocker outside of BrightBridge control)
- Proposed credit: 100k tokens attached to BrightBridge sandbox
- Extension dates: +45 days from the current POC end date (or opt-in 30 day + review at 30 days)
- Acceptance criteria (see Karthik’s note)

Marissa — can you confirm the paperwork timeline and whether we need a signed amendment vs. internal approval? If procurement can provide a one‑page approval (signer name + date + PO if required) we can faster-route it.

Sara — if you can reply with the target end date you’d prefer (30 vs 45) and a primary contact for PO processing, I’ll accelerate the internal ticket. If procurement wants a short SOW addendum I can draft it and send for review.

I’ve added the HubSpot deal and Drive links to the metadata for procurement.

Best,
David
David Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
